name: District Expenditures by Function Code
offers: GEN_FUND and GRNTS_REVOLV separately, by function code, per district, 2009-2025. The fund split rule 11 says nobody publishes.

name: District Expenditures by Spending Category
offers: Supersedes dese_measure on coverage: 421 districts against 7, and agrees with it exactly where they overlap.

name: School Expenditures by Spending Category
offers: Per-SCHOOL spending. The only per-school financial series in this archive.

name: Where Residents Go to School (Sending)
offers: Where resident children go, by receiving district and reason, 2014-2026. Closes "how many children leave and for where".

name: Reasons for Student Enrollment by Town (Receiving)
offers: Who arrives and from where. The mirror of the sending file; together they give a NET choice position.

name: Special Education Circuit Breaker Reimbursements
offers: A fund rule 11 names as unmapped, AND a count of children: ELIG_STU_CLAIM_CNT.
refresh_note: Keys on FY, not SY. Every other file here is school year.

name: Chapter 70 Foundation Budget and Net School Spending
offers: Required against actual net school spending. Lunenburg sits at ~128% of the floor.
refresh_note: Stops at SY2022. The Chapter 70 profile workbook below runs to FY2026.

name: Elementary and Secondary Teachers by Grade and Subject
offers: FTE by grade band AND subject AND school. Breaks a limit recorded as structural: grade detail without FTE, or FTE without grade detail, never both.
refresh_note: Carries a State row and a SUBJ of All beside detail. Establish levels before summing.

name: Elementary and Secondary Teachers by Program Area
offers: GEN_ED / SPED / CAREER_TECH / EL teacher FTE, per school.
refresh_note: Lunenburg SPED FTE falls 18.5 (2008) to 2.0 (2026) while total FTE holds flat. That is the signature of recoding, not of staff leaving. UNRESOLVED.

name: Elementary and Secondary Teacher Data
offers: Teacher counts, student-teacher ratio, licensure, experience, in-field share.

name: Total Educators, Retention, and New Hires
offers: Headcount by job class INCLUDING Administrator and Paraprofessional, plus hires and retention. 2021-2023 only.
refresh_note: Headcount, not FTE. Administrators 28->38 over three years on a base of ten people; a reclassification would look identical.

name: Special Education Indicators
offers: A published COUNT of students with disabilities, 217-265, plus sped staffing ratios.
refresh_note: Its paraprofessional ratio times the count implies $69,161 per FTE against the district budget line. The two are not the same population. UNRESOLVED.

name: Special Education Program Characteristics and Student Demographics
offers: Disability type and demographics behind the SWD count.

name: Special Education Placement Trajectory
offers: Where a child starts against where they end up. The route into out-of-district.
refresh_note: Tiny bases. 14.3% of 28 is four children; the percentage must never travel alone.

name: Students Moving In and Out of Special Education Services
offers: Caseload dynamics: how many enter and leave services each year.
refresh_note: SY2024 and SY2025 are identical across all four columns. Probably a carried-forward row; check before quoting either.

name: Enrollment: Grade, Race/Ethnicity, Gender, and Selected Populations
offers: Enrollment by grade and school. The denominators for most of the above.

name: Chapter 70 District Profile
offers: 34 years of the Chapter 70 formula, FY1993-FY2026 — foundation enrollment, foundation budget, required local contribution, aid, required and actual NSS. FY2026 aid reconciles exactly to the figure derived independently for /state-aid.
refresh_note: The Socrata page qt58-634r has NO DOWNLOAD and redirects here. Read with data_only=True and take the DataC70 sheet; the front sheet is a VLOOKUP interface.

name: Chapter 70 Key Factors
offers: Foundation enrollment split by English learner, vocational and low-income share — the formula INPUTS, which is what lets anybody model how it responds to enrollment change.
refresh_note: Data sheets are dataAid, dataNSS, dataContribution. Front sheet is an interface.

name: Job Classification Codes (evaluation)
offers: 43 code/label pairs -- 1200 Superintendent, 1305 Principal and so on. The vocabulary behind EPIMS job classification.
refresh_note: Covers the EVALUATION job classes: administrators and licensed staff. Contains NO paraprofessional codes, so it does not by itself resolve the paraprofessional boundary.

name: SIMS Data Handbook (current)
offers: Defines STUDENT data: special education placement, school choice. 42 mentions of special education, 6 of placement.
refresh_note: Contains NO staffing definitions — checked with word boundaries after raw substring counts said otherwise. The staffing definitions are in EPIMS, which is NOT YET HELD and is what would resolve both open contradictions.

name: EPIMS Data Handbook
offers: RESOLVES the paraprofessional contradiction: FTE is per ASSIGNMENT, not per person, so DESE FTE and the district budget line have different denominators. AND reveals that EPIMS collects per-individual Federal Salary Source plus percent of salary — which fund pays which post, the thing rule 11 says nobody publishes.
refresh_note: Federal grants only; state grants and revolving funds are not in these fields.

name: SIMS Data Handbook 2021
offers: As above, 2021 edition.

name: SIMS Data Handbook 2022
offers: As above, 2022 edition.

name: EPIMS federal salary source, aggregated by job classification
offers: EPIMS collects per-individual federal grant funding percentages. Aggregated by job classification this answers which fund pays which post — rule 11 outright. No individual records sought.

name: Non-Public School Enrollment
offers: Children leaving to PRIVATE school. The choice files capture public-to-public only, so this is the missing half of who leaves.

name: Class Size
offers: What staffing changes did to classrooms — the thing residents actually feel.

name: Mental Health Staff by District
offers: The town cut a school psychologist to zero; this is that category.

name: Educators by Age Group
offers: Retirement exposure, which drives salary-step cost.

name: Collaborative Placement
offers: Collaborative is one of the three out-of-district categories in our placement counts.
